request.spec:
Live due now rounds half to even (1.025 becomes 1.02, 1.035 becomes 1.04). A settled claim keeps
its frozen figure. Every due-total is now the sum of the already-rounded claim figures, not the
rounded total amount times the rate; a person with nothing that counts shows 0.00. A person whose
grade has no rate today still shows n/a even with nothing that counts (n/a wins over 0.00), unless
a settled claim keeps a figure: then the total is the sum of the figures there are. The sheet's
due-total is still everyone's due-total added up.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Live due now rounds half to even (1.025 becomes 1.02, 1.035 becomes 1.04). A settled claim keeps
its frozen figure. Every due-total is now the sum of the already-rounded claim figures, not the
rounded total amount times the rate; a person with nothing that counts shows 0.00. A person whose
grade has no rate today still shows n/a even with nothing that counts (n/a wins over 0.00), unless

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I made the change, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 acceptance tests.

**Rounding:** a live due now rounds half to even, so 1.025 becomes 1.02 and 1.035 becomes 1.04. I changed this in the screen (`dueOn` in `rates/rates.ts`) and on the server (`ClaimService.dueOn`, now `HALF_EVEN`). Claims settled before this change keep the figure stored when they were settled. A claim settled from now on gets the half-to-even figure, the same one it showed while live.

**Person due-total** (`people/people.ts`): this is now the sum of the rounded figures of the person's claims that count (open or settled). A settled claim adds its stored figure; a live claim adds its due at the rate in force on the claim's date.
- With nothing that counts, it shows 0.00.
- If the person's grade has no rate today, it shows n/a, even with nothing that counts. The exception is when a settled claim has a stored figure: then it adds up whatever figures exist.

Live claims that show n/a are left out of the sum. The sheet's due-total is still the sum of everyone's due-totals, leaving out anyone who shows n/a.

One interpretation to check: in the no-rate-today case, I read "the sum of the figures there are" as also counting live claims whose own date has a rate, not only the stored settled figures. The tests pass this way, but if you meant only the stored figures, it's a one-line change.

The stored data needed no new migration, because the stored settled figures stay as they are.
